- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct — but often overcorrects, leading to prolonged overestimation.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: forecasts drift toward historical averages too quickly, missing short-term volatility.
- In periods of high volatility or sharp price movements, model underreacts to recent data, lagging behind true price action.
- Model tends to underestimate prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when true prices show downward momentum.
- Model exhibits “overconfidence” in early forecast days — forecasts are often too high relative to recent history, especially when recent prices are falling.
- When true prices are trending downward, model often fails to adjust downward quickly, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model underestimates prices when recent history shows a clear downward trend, especially if the trend is sustained for 5+ days.
- Model tends to overestimate prices in the middle of the forecast horizon (days 10–20) when true prices are stabilizing or reversing.
- Model often fails to capture short-term reversals — especially when true prices drop sharply after a peak, model continues to hold high forecasts.
